## Rate limits

Each key gets **60 requests per minute** sustained, with bursts up to **10**.
Exceeding it returns `42

9 RATE_LIMITED` with a `Retry-After` header (in
seconds):

```http theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many R

equests
Retry-After: 7

{ "code": "RATE_LIMITED", "message": "API key rate limit exceeded. Slow down and retry." }
```

Honor `Retry-After`, add jittered exponential backoff, and expect these limits
to be tuned during the preview.

Other `429`
s — the per-minute brakes and daily budgets described with the\nendpoints below — carry `Retry-After` whenever the refusal knows w
hen it\nlifts, which is the ordinary case. Treat it as a hint that is usually there\nrather than a guarantee: a refusal that reach

es you without one still needs
your backoff, so **never** block waiting for a header that may not come.

## Endpoints

Each e
ndpoint is fully documented — request and response schemas, examples,\nand an interactive playground — under **Endpoints** in the

sidebar.

**Catalog** — discover the IDs everything else takes:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET /me` | The acc
ount behind the key |\n| `GET /organizations` | The organizations the caller belongs to — where `organizationId` comes from. A key
is bound to one organization and only ever sees that one |\n| `GET /projects` | Projects the key can access (optionally `?organiz
ationId=`) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers` | The project's saved MCP servers |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers/{ser
verId}/revisions` | A server's stored revisions, newest first: captures of its tools and server info, recorded whenever they chang
e (`?limit=&cursor=`) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions/{revisionNumber}` | One revision: every tool's
definition and the server info it reported. Fields listed in `droppedFields` were too large to store, so they are unknown, not abs
ent |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions/{revisionNumber}/diff` | What changed since the revision before,
or since `?from=`: tools added, removed and changed, and server info changes with both values. A field listed in `droppedFields.fr
om` or `droppedFields.to` was not stored on that side, so a change to it is unknown |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites` |
The project's eval suites, with latest-run summaries |\n| `GET`, `POST /projects/{projectId}/clients` | List clients, or create o
ne from a template or full config |\n| `GET`, `PATCH`, `DELETE /projects/{projectId}/clients/{client}` | Read, edit, or delete a c
lient. The path segment takes a client **name or ID** |\n| `POST /projects/{projectId}/clients/{client}/servers` | Replace the cli
ent's server attachments (a replacement — omitted servers are detached) |\n| `POST /projects/{projectId}/clients/{client}/duplicat
e` | Copy a client's current config into a new client |\n| `GET /chat-sessions` | Chat sessions (`?projectId=&status=&limit=&befor

e=`) |

**Project environments** — the named execution bundles (one host, optionally a
standalone server group, optionally pinn
ed skills and plugin versions) that eval\nsuites and goals run against. Reads need project membership; **every write\nneeds projec
t admin**. Writes are revisioned: pass the `revision` you last read\nback as `expectedRevision`, and a stale value returns `CONFLI

CT` (409) instead
of overwriting a concurrent edit.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET`, `POST /projects/{projectI
d}/environments` | List environments (`?includeArchived=true` to include archived ones), or create one |\n| `GET`, `PATCH /project
s/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}` | Read one environment, or edit it (send `null` to clear `serverAttachmentId`, `skillS
election`, or `pluginVersionIds`) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/resolve` | Preview the host config,
closed server set, and pinned plugin versions this environment resolves to right now |\n| `POST /projects/{projectId}/environment
s/{environmentId}/archive` | Archive it — reversible, and frees the name for a new one |\n| `POST /projects/{projectId}/environmen
ts/{environmentId}/restore` | Restore an archived environment |\n\nArchive and restore are explicit sub-actions rather than a `DEL
ETE` because the\nrow is kept and restore has real semantics: it re-checks the name and drops\nplugin pins whose version no longer

exists.

**Server diagnostics & primitives** (`/projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/...`):

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |\n| `POST .../validate` | Connect, initialize, and capture a capability snapshot |\n| `POST .../doctor` | Full health wor
kflow: probe → connect → initialize → capabilities |\n| `POST .../check-oauth` | Does this server require an OAuth grant? |\n| `PO
ST .../tools` | List the server's tools |\n| `POST .../tools/call` | Execute a tool; returns the MCP `CallToolResult` plus additiv
e `durationMs`, and `authChallenge` when the result asks for sign-in (see [Sign-in challenges](#sign-in-challenges)) |\n| `POST ..
./prompts` | List the server's prompts |\n| `POST .../prompts/get` | Render a prompt; returns the MCP `GetPromptResult` verbatim |

| `POST .../resources` | List the server's resources |
| `POST .../resources/read` | Read one resource by URI |
| `POST .../ex
port` | One JSON snapshot of tools, resources, and prompts |\n| `GET`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE .../accounts[/{account}]` | The ser
ver's accounts. See [Server accounts](#server-accounts) |\n| `POST .../oauth/import-tokens` | **Deprecated.** Uploads to your defa
ult account; use `PUT .../accounts/{account}`. See [The deprecated import route](#the-deprecated-import-route) |\n\n**Eval runs**

(`/projects/{projectId}/...`):

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../eval-suites` | Author-only: create a suite +
its test cases from `name` + `serverIds` + a default `model` + `tests`, WITHOUT running it; responds `201` + `suiteId`. Each test
's case body is an ordered `steps` array (prompt / toolCall / interact / assert); per-test `model`/`provider`/`runs` are optional
and fall back to suite defaults |\n| `POST .../eval-runs` | Create a run from a `suiteId` (rerun; `serverIds` optional — defaults
to the suite's saved servers) or `suiteName` + inline `tests` + `serverIds` (new suite). `environmentId` (requires `suiteId`) runs
against one of the suite's attached environments instead. Responds `202` + `runId` |\n| `PATCH .../eval-suites/{suiteId}` | Edit
suite settings, including `environmentIds` — the project environments the suite runs against (non-empty array sets/replaces, `null
` clears) |\n| `PATCH .../eval-suites/{suiteId}/schedule` | Enable/disable scheduled runs; `environmentId` pins which environment
they launch |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}` | Run status, result, and summary — poll until terminal. Carries `gateWaiver`: the au
dited override in force over this run's gate, or `null` |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/gate` | The stored suite quality-gate repo
rt for this run (`passed` / `failed` / `non_gateable` / `not_configured`). `not_configured` is a 200 report, never a missing route
. A deployment that predates the evaluator answers `422 FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED` |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/decision-summary` |
**Start here when a run did not pass.** The canonical run decision contract: the verdict and where it came from, counts labelled
with the population they count, the run's own verdict decision, and per-trial diagnostics with the user-value chain, the first fai
led stage, the failure category, evidence scoped to that stage, and one next action (paginated) |\n| `POST .../eval-runs/{runId}/g
ate-waivers` | Override a **failing** run's release gate until `expiresAt` (required, future, max 30 days out), with a `reason` (r
